title: C# .NET and Oracle Backend Exercises
description: Practise each step of the Reading List API. Read the code, find mistakes and explain the reply. C# and Oracle tasks run in the local sample, so use the lesson setup and compare your work with the notes.

exercises.question: A reader clicks Add book. Which part checks the title and asks Oracle to save it?
exercises.explanation: The browser sends the request. The C# API checks its values and talks to Oracle. Oracle keeps the row. The browser does not need the database password.
options: The page heading
The C# API running on the server
The CSS file

exercises.question: You want the controller-based API used in this course. Which project command should replace line 2?
exercises.explanation: The webapi template with --use-controllers makes an API project with controllers. -f net10.0 chooses .NET 10. A console project is useful for small programs, but it does not create this web API setup.
exercises.code:
dotnet --list-sdks
dotnet new console -n ReadingListApi -f net10.0
options: dotnet new webapi --use-controllers -n ReadingListApi -f net10.0
dotnet new classlib -n ReadingListApi -f net10.0
dotnet clean

exercises.question: The API reads a setting called ConnectionStrings:Oracle. In an environment variable, replace the colon with ___, so the key is ConnectionStrings__Oracle.
exercises.explanation: Use two underscores: __. .NET reads them as a separator between setting levels. The value belongs in the API's environment, not in browser JavaScript or a public file.

exercises.question: The table uses the rule below. What happens when this INSERT tries to save is_read as 2?
exercises.explanation: The CHECK rule permits only 0 or 1. A value of 2 fails the check, so Oracle does not add this row. The rule protects the table even if a program sends a wrong value.
exercises.code:
-- This rule is part of reading_list_books:
-- CHECK (is_read IN (0, 1))
INSERT INTO reading_list_books (title, is_read)
VALUES ('Moon Trip', 2);
options: Oracle silently changes 2 to 1
Oracle saves 2 because it is a number
Oracle rejects the row because 2 fails the check

exercises.question: In a .NET 10 scratch file, add rules to this request model: Title is required and may have at most 120 characters. Use DataAnnotations attributes. Then compare your work with the solution.
exercises.explanation: Required rejects missing, empty and whitespace-only titles. StringLength(120) sets the maximum length. The sample's [ApiController] checks model errors and returns 400 before a controller action uses invalid input.

exercises.question: This code has a connection string, but the connection is still closed. Which step belongs before ExecuteReaderAsync?
exercises.explanation: Creating an OracleConnection does not open it. Await OpenAsync before running a command. using releases the connection when the work ends, including when an error occurs.
options: Put the database password in the SQL text
await connection.OpenAsync();
Remove the SELECT word

exercises.question: A controller has [Route("api/books")]. Add [Http___] to its list action so GET /api/books can reach it.
exercises.explanation: HttpGet tells ASP.NET Core that this action handles GET requests. The controller's route supplies api/books. A method name alone is not the complete route rule.

exercises.question: The reading list has no books yet. What should GET /api/books return?
exercises.explanation: The collection exists even when it has no rows. Return 200 with an empty JSON array, []. A missing single book, such as GET /api/books/999 when that id is absent, is a different case and gets 404.
options: 200 OK with []
404 for the whole API
201 Created with an invented book

exercises.question: The API accepts this valid request and saves one new row. Which reply matches this course's POST route?
exercises.explanation: POST creates a new book. The API returns 201, the saved book, and a Location header pointing to its address. Read the returned id; do not guess that it will be 1.
options: 204 with no new book address
404 because the id was not sent
201 with the new book and a Location header

exercises.question: This DELETE command would remove every book. Change it so it removes only the row whose id is in bookId. Use a named :id parameter. This is a code fragment for the sample's open Oracle connection.
exercises.explanation: DELETE without WHERE affects every row. WHERE id = :id selects one id. BindByName makes the value match the name, and an Int64 parameter carries the C# long id as data.
checklist: The SQL ends with WHERE id = :id.
An OracleDbType.Int64 parameter named id receives bookId.
The command uses ExecuteNonQueryAsync after the parameter is added.

exercises.question: A fresh connection starts a transaction, inserts a practice book, then rolls back before any commit. What happens to that inserted row?
exercises.explanation: Rollback cancels changes made in that transaction, so this new row does not remain. Identity numbers can still have gaps. Rollback does not promise to give an id number back.
options: The title changes to an empty string
The inserted row is undone; its id number may still be skipped
The API must delete every row in the table

exercises.question: A POST reply gives your new test book id 37. What is the best next step when testing the complete route flow?
exercises.explanation: Use the id or Location from the real response. Read that book, update it, delete it, and check that reading the deleted id gives 404. Another run can receive a different id.
options: GET /api/books/37 and check the saved title
Always GET /api/books/1
Wait one second and assume the save worked

exercises.question: This browser code is the wrong place for a database secret. What should the browser do instead?
exercises.explanation: Browser files can be read by the person using the page. Keep the Oracle connection setting in the API process. The browser sends HTTP requests to /api/books; it never opens the Oracle connection.
options: Hide the password in a CSS file
Send a request to the API and let the API talk to Oracle
Rename oraclePassword to a shorter name

exercises.question: Finishing the local practice checks means this unauthenticated teaching API is ready for anyone on the internet to change its books.
exercises.explanation: False. This sample is a local learning project. Before making a real shared service, plan who may read and change data, protect secrets, use HTTPS, and add suitable access checks, error handling, backups and tests.
